rationale:
SPLIT, by reusing two comparator-accepted checkpoints whose frozen Lean types are byte-identical to what the supplied proof needs. This creates no new DAG nodes.

What the children cover in the supplied proof:
- Step 1 (G is C^1 on Bo, so x -> A(x) := DG(x) is continuous; |A(x)v| >= |v|) is child `graph_chart_immersion`. This is `Submission.rsod_graphChart_injective_contDiffOn_fderiv_injective`, accepted node root.regular_set_open_dense-a1.c1_submanifold_graph_ball-a1.graph_chart_immersion-a1, candidate 97c0c4bc. It gives injectivity of A(x) instead of the bound |A(x)v| >= |v|. The supplied proof uses that bound only in step 3, to make N(x) = A(x)#A(x) injective, and injectivity of A(x) suffices: <N v, v> = |A v|^2.
- Steps 2-4 (hand-built adjoint; the Gram operator is a unit; Ring.inverse is continuous at units; the projection formula via eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero) are child `projection_continuity`. This is `Submission.aetp_starProjection_range_continuousOn`, accepted node root.tilt_excess_height_estimate-a1.ae_tangent_planes-a1.projection_continuity-a1, candidate 9f89be4c. It is exactly the same argument, stated for every injective L instead of the family A(x).

Parent assembly (supplied step 5 plus composition), with G(z) = graphPoint z (u z):
(a) Apply child 1 with q := LinearIsometryEquiv.refl, x0 := 0 and Omega := ball 0 R, which is open. Since refl y + 0 = y, its map is G, so G is C^1 on the ball and DG(x) is injective for every x in the ball.
(b) ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen makes x -> DG(x) continuous on the ball.
(c) Child 2 composed with (b) (ContinuousOn.comp, MapsTo from (a)) makes x -> (range DG(x)).starProjection continuous on the ball.
(d) Submodule.starProjection_map_apply plus ext give (map Q K).starProjection = Q o K.starProjection o Q.symm. The map x -> Q o P(x) o Q.symm is continuous on the ball (ContinuousOn.clm_comp with constants), and ContinuousOn.congr gives the exact frozen claim.

Lean checks (scratch build of the frozen Submission; the problem's `main_theorem` sorry is the only sorry):
- Assembly.lean proves the exact frozen parent type from the two exact child types.
- Full.lean uses the real accepted proofs taken from the candidate commits, including their merged helper rsod_graphPoint_eq_finAddEquivProd_symm. `#print axioms` for the parent gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and the same for both children.
- validate_lean_statement accepts both child types.
- In gmt-compare contract mode, the NodeChallenge modules for both children and the parent elaborate against the frozen build. The NodeSolution modules elaborate against a scratch Submission containing the proofs.

Controller checks:
- _existing_lean_name_problem allows a cross-branch name when the type is identical and the node is an accepted checkpoint. Each name occurs on exactly one node, status accepted, with a candidate_commit.
- The ids map to those existing nodes, so the new-node count is 0.
- _install_parent_supplied_child_handoff returns early for accepted checkpoints, and _solve resumes the accepted candidate.
- This run already has more than 40 such cross-branch reuses.
- max_nodes is now 1000 with 266 nodes in use. Depth 3 is below max_depth 6.

Why not finer or coarser:
- Step 5 is a few lines and stays in the parent. A node for it would add overhead without reusable value.
- Not splitting would force the parent to re-prove about 110 lines of already-accepted Lean. Checkpoints from other branches only become usable once declared as children.

No public sources were needed. The projection formula L(L^T L)^{-1}L^T is standard linear algebra, and both children are already kernel-checked.

subproblems.title: The rotated, translated graph chart of a C^1 map is an injective C^1 immersion
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, q a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l) = Amb n l = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)), u : R^n -> R^l a map, x0 a point of R^(n+l), and Omega an open subset of R^n on which u is C^1. Put phi(x) := q(graphPoint x (u x)) + x0, where graphPoint x y is the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of x and whose last l coordinates are those of y. Then (i) phi is injective on all of R^n, (ii) phi is C^1 on Omega, and (iii) for every x in Omega the Frechet derivative fderiv R phi x : R^n -> R^(n+l) is injective.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (x₀ : Amb n ℓ) (Ω : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen Ω → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u Ω → Function.Injective (fun x => q (graphPoint x (u x)) + x₀) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun x => q (graphPoint x (u x)) + x₀) Ω ∧ ∀ x ∈ Ω, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (fun x => q (graphPoint x (u x)) + x₀) x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. E := Amb n l = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)). phi(x) := q(graphPoint x (u x)) + x0. S : E ≃L[R] Rn n × Rn l is Mathlib's EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd, the coordinate-splitting continuous linear equivalence. Its inverse S.symm (x, y) is the vector whose coordinate at Fin.castAdd l j is x j (j in Fin n) and at Fin.natAdd n k is y k (k in Fin l), because S reindexes along finSumFinEquiv, which sends Sum.inl j to Fin.castAdd l j and Sum.inr k to Fin.natAdd n k.

1. graphPoint is S.symm. For all x in Rn n and y in Rn l, graphPoint x y = S.symm (x, y). Compare coordinates: every index of Fin (n+l) is Fin.castAdd l j or Fin.natAdd n k (Fin.addCases).
- At Fin.castAdd l j, the left side is Fin.append x y (Fin.castAdd l j) = x j (Fin.append_left), and the right side is x j by the description of S.symm.
- At Fin.natAdd n k, both sides equal y k (Fin.append_right and the description of S.symm).
So the two vectors are equal.

2. The linear part. Let A := q ∘L S.symm : Rn n × Rn l ->L[R] E, with q viewed as a continuous linear map. A is injective, as the composite of the injective maps S.symm and q. By step 1, phi(x) = A(x, u x) + x0 for every x in Rn n.

3. phi is injective on all of Rn n. Suppose phi(x) = phi(x'). Cancelling x0 gives A(x, u x) = A(x', u x'). Injectivity of A gives (x, u x) = (x', u x'), and comparing first components gives x = x'. This is conjunct (i).

4. phi is C^1 on Omega. The map x -> (x, u x) is C^1 on Omega, because the identity is smooth and u is C^1 on Omega (ContDiffOn.prodMk). A is a continuous linear map, hence C^infinity, so x -> A(x, u x) is C^1 on Omega (ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn). Adding the constant x0 keeps it C^1 (ContDiffOn.add with contDiffOn_const). This is conjunct (ii).

5. The derivative at a point of Omega. Fix x in Omega and write Du(x) := fderiv R u x.
- Omega is open, so it is a neighbourhood of x. Hence u is C^1 at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt), so differentiable at x since 1 ≠ 0, and u has derivative Du(x) at x.
- So z -> (z, u z) has derivative (ContinuousLinearMap.id).prod Du(x) at x.
- The continuous linear map A is its own derivative, and the constant x0 contributes nothing.
- By the chain rule, phi has derivative A ∘L (id.prod Du(x)) at x. So fderiv R phi x v = A(v, Du(x) v) for every v in Rn n.

6. The derivative is injective. Suppose fderiv R phi x v = fderiv R phi x w. By step 5, A(v, Du(x) v) = A(w, Du(x) w). Injectivity of A gives (v, Du(x) v) = (w, Du(x) w), so v = w. Thus fderiv R phi x is injective for every x in Omega. This is conjunct (iii).

Steps 3, 4 and 6 prove the three conjuncts of the statement.
proof_key_steps: graphPoint x y = EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd.symm (x, y), by comparing coordinates on Fin.castAdd / Fin.natAdd indices
phi(x) = A(x, u x) + x0 with A = q ∘L finAddEquivProd.symm an injective continuous linear map
phi is injective: cancel x0, use injectivity of A, compare first components
phi is C^1 on Omega: A composed with the C^1 map x ↦ (x, u x), plus a constant
chain rule at x in the open set Omega: Dphi(x) v = A(v, Du(x) v)
Dphi(x) is injective because A is injective; compare first components

subproblems.title: Continuity of the orthogonal projection onto the range of an injective linear map
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, F := R^n = Rn n and E := R^(n+l) = Amb n l (Euclidean spaces). Consider the map that sends a continuous linear map L : F -> E to the orthogonal projection of E onto the subspace range L, viewed as a continuous linear endomorphism of E ((LinearMap.range L).starProjection). Both spaces of continuous linear maps carry their operator-norm topologies. This map is continuous on the set of injective L.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), ContinuousOn (fun L : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ => (LinearMap.range L.toLinearMap).starProjection) {L : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ | Function.Injective L}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation.
- F := Rn n and E := Amb n l. Both are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, hence complete.
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i in Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of F, so every v in F equals sum_i v_i e_i with v_i = <e_i, v> (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr for EuclideanSpace.basisFun, basisFun_apply).
- For L in F ->L[R] E, range L is a finite-dimensional, hence complete, subspace of E. So it has an orthogonal projection, and (range L).starProjection in E ->L[R] E is that projection.
- S := {L | L injective}.
- The endomorphism ring F ->L[R] F has multiplication = composition and 1 = id. It is a complete normed ring.

1. Hand-built transpose. For L in F ->L[R] E let L# := sum_i (innerSL R (L e_i)).smulRight e_i, in E ->L[R] F. So L# w = sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i. For all w in E and v in F:
<L# w, v> = sum_i <L e_i, w> <e_i, v> = sum_i <L e_i, w> v_i = <w, sum_i v_i L e_i> = <w, L v>.
This uses bilinearity and symmetry of the real inner product, <e_i, v> = v_i, and linearity of L applied to v = sum_i v_i e_i.

2. The transpose is continuous in L. For each i:
- L -> L e_i is continuous: it is evaluation at a fixed vector, a continuous linear map of L.
- innerSL R is a continuous linear map.
- phi -> phi.smulRight e_i is continuous: it is the continuous linear map smulRightL R E F followed by evaluation at the fixed vector e_i.
A finite sum of continuous maps is continuous, so L -> L# is continuous on all of F ->L[R] E.

3. The Gram operator. Put N(L) := L# ∘L L in F ->L[R] F. Composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous (Continuous.clm_comp), so L -> N(L) is continuous.
If L is injective, then N(L) is a unit:
- Suppose N(L) v = 0. By step 1 with w = L v: <L v, L v> = <L#(L v), v> = <N(L) v, v> = <0, v> = 0.
- So L v = 0, and v = 0 by injectivity. Hence ker N(L) = 0.
- An endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space F with trivial kernel is a unit of the endomorphism ring (LinearMap.isUnit_iff_ker_eq_bot, transferred by ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_iff_isUnit_toLinearMap).
The argument is uniform in n, including n = 0, where F = 0.

4. Projection formula. For every L put P(L) := L ∘L (Ring.inverse N(L)) ∘L L#, in E ->L[R] E. Claim: if L is injective, then (range L).starProjection = P(L).
Fix w in E and let y := P(L) w = L(Ring.inverse N(L) (L# w)). Then:
- y lies in range L.
- By step 3, N(L) is a unit, so N(L) * Ring.inverse N(L) = 1 (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel). Applying this identity to L# w gives L#(L(Ring.inverse N(L) (L# w))) = L# w, that is, L# y = L# w.
- For every element L v of range L, step 1 gives <w - y, L v> = <L#(w - y), v> = <L# w - L# y, v> = <0, v> = 0.
By the characterization of orthogonal projections (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero: if y is in K and <w - y, k> = 0 for all k in K, then K.starProjection w = y), (range L).starProjection w = y = P(L) w. As w was arbitrary, the two continuous linear maps are equal (ext).

5. The formula is continuous at each injective L0. By step 3, N(L0) = ↑u0 for some unit u0.
- Ring.inverse is continuous at every unit of the complete normed ring F ->L[R] F (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt u0).
- Composing with the continuous map L -> N(L) (step 3), L -> Ring.inverse N(L) is continuous at L0.
- L -> L# is continuous (step 2), L -> L is continuous, and composition is jointly continuous (ContinuousAt.clm_comp).
Therefore L -> P(L) = L ∘L (Ring.inverse N(L) ∘L L#), which is defined for every L, is continuous at L0.

6. Conclusion. Let f(L) := (range L).starProjection and let L0 be in S.
- By step 5, P is continuous at L0, hence continuous within S at L0.
- By step 4, f(L) = P(L) for every L in S, and f(L0) = P(L0).
- So f is continuous within S at L0 (ContinuousWithinAt.congr).
Since L0 in S was arbitrary, f is continuous on S. This is the statement.
proof_key_steps: hand-built transpose L# w = Σ_i ⟨L e_i, w⟩ e_i satisfies ⟨L# w, v⟩ = ⟨w, L v⟩ and is continuous in L
Gram operator N(L) = L# ∘L L is continuous in L, and a unit of End(R^n) when L is injective, since ⟨N(L) v, v⟩ = |L v|^2
for injective L, (range L).starProjection = L ∘L Ring.inverse N(L) ∘L L#, via Ring.mul_inverse_cancel and eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero
Ring.inverse is continuous at units (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt), so the formula is continuous at each injective L0
ContinuousWithinAt.congr on the set of injective maps gives ContinuousOn
